verdict.rationale: Honcho is a memory-layer service, not an agent, so an official MCP server is a fair axis. Its own docs describe a first-party Honcho MCP server, hosted at mcp.honcho.dev and also runnable locally over stdio, Streamable HTTP, or Docker, which any MCP-compatible tool can connect to. Missing for 10: documentation of the specific MCP tools and auth setup in the evidence, and independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting an agent.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: The Honcho MCP server gives any MCP-compatible AI tool persistent memory and personalization.
Skip `mcp.honcho.dev` and run the MCP server locally over stdio, Streamable HTTP, or Docker.
every AI tool you use — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, your own agent — reads the same understanding of who you are.
